Abyssal Tether 3D · Chapter II

LAMPHOLD

“Every lamp a bed. Every bed a morning.” A town of three thousand lamps, one headless office that answers bells, and a door that does not want to open.

  • 500 mof descent, 600 → 1,100 m
  • 7beats, one boss exam
  • ~26.5 minfirst descent on Normal
  • 3difficulties
  • Freewith Chapter I
The field manual

Level Two at a glance

Chapter I taught you the rope. Chapter II teaches you that the rope can move: the rings swing, ride, lift and fall, and something in a black suit listens to every bell you ring. You are not asked to fight it. You are asked to put the sound where you are not.

The story in one breath

The Lampholders settled the pit below the Mark. They refused the Keepers' law BELOW THIS MARK NO LAMPS and lit three thousand lamps, because “one lamp holds one of them.” Every sleeper is kept in a niche above their own bed, with an arm raised, holding their own lamp. Each evening the town is put to bed, tier by tier. Tonight the Lamplighter is late, the Evening is not, and you are carrying the brightest lamp in the world.

What is new since Chapter I

  • Moving anchors: pendulum chandeliers, a counterweight lift, the Great Bell and the Span's trolleys.
  • Stand-on lifts that carry you.
  • The Usher: it answers bells, and the Head Usher, the Doorman, is the chapter's boss exam.
  • A town of lamps that is put out tier by tier.
  • Five Names to find, a chapter radio, and a hook into Chapter III.
Chapter 1 of this manual

Before you descend

Start Lamphold from the menu (Choose your descent › II · Lamphold), from the Chapter II · Lamphold button on Chapter I's end card, or with ?chapter=2 in the address. Continue always returns to the chapter and beat you left.

Quest controllers

Right stick← → smooth turn · ↑ ↓ reel in / out.

Habit worth building

Walking with a gun out is 20% slower and a gun left alone on the ground goes back to its holster after 3.5 s. A trigger press always draws first, then fires: hold the button through the draw or the shot is cancelled.

The rope, the recharge and the grip

Each rope launcher recharges after a shot (default 1.5 s; the wrist bars show it; set it to 0 in Settings › Rope for no wait). The rope is a spring with a slip clutch, reeling in on a loaded line costs grip on Nightmare and Abyss, and your free hand can climb your own line. Edges tire the grip faster than chalk-studded stone; standing on the ground refills it.

Chapter 2 of this manual

The new rules of Lamphold

1 · Live anchors

Some rings swing: a chandelier on a 36 m chain in II·1, five more in II·3. Your rope takes the anchor's velocity. Fire as the ring comes toward you; let go as it rises; you keep its speed.

2 · Carriers

A lift that is flagged as a carrier carries you while you stand on it: your height follows the cage after every physics step. The lift of the Street of Doors and the chain platform of the Soot Throat work this way.

3 · Pull rings

Some rings move machinery. Hook one and yank (F on desktop; the grip on a tethered hand in VR). The counterweight lift of the Street of Doors is the first.

4 · The exam's machines

The Great Bell is a 30 m pendulum with a stroke every six seconds. Two trolleys run under the Span at 7 and 9 m/s. The cage is a lift that goes down 33 m. They run on a fixed rhythm, so what you learn repeats.

5 · The Evening

Once the Usher has answered the bell, the lamps above you start to go out: a front that follows about 90 m behind you, and 40 m behind in the exam. The radio's bars are the lit lamps near you; they drop with them.

6 · Names

Five slabs carry a Name each. You find one by standing at it; the first two lie behind doors that open to a knock. The end card counts them.

Bells call it

The Usher's rule

The Usher answers bells. Where its cold light falls, it strikes. Put the bell where you are not.

The Usher does not read you. It has no idea where you stand. It hears tolls, points its ring at where the toll was (plus where the toll is going), draws a sphere of cold light there and strikes the sphere. You are in danger only while you stand in the sphere of a toll you made.

TollWhat makes itLoudnessHeard within
BellRinging a bell: swing a rope ring into it1.060 m
Great BellThe Evening's stroke in the Well1.0the whole Well
GongThe cage gong, the pawl clunk, a gong plate0.848 m
MachineA haul, a pull, a winch ratchet that clanks0.742 m
CrashPlates of the Span falling0.636 m
Brass ringBiting a brass ring (it chimes)0.3518 m

An Usher ignores your footsteps, landings, breath and door knocks. A toll is masked only by a strictly louder toll within 10 m, so a bigger bell can hide a small one.

What an Usher does, in order

  1. Listen
    Hears a toll. Pale wide sphere. A newer toll re-aims it.
  2. Coil
    The sphere tightens. The last 0.4 s is commit (gold): the aim is frozen.
  3. Whip
    The throat lunges. Lethal inside the sphere only.
  4. Recoil
    Your guaranteed safe window. It cannot coil again.

You can read all of it: the sphere's size, a hum that rises, a hum that jumps, the captions below, and the rope buzz: the hand whose line is on a ring inside an Usher's sphere buzzes, faintly while it listens, more as it coils and solid when it commits. The sphere's centre never moves in the last 0.4 s, and nothing is lethal during the grace period after you wake.

Captions you will see

CaptionWhat it is
[Three light, even raps]knock
[Breath through a pipe]throat
[Hum rising]ring
[Throat whips]lunge
[Hum jumps]commit
[A long breath out]recoil
[A lamp goes out]snuff
[Ring chimes]chime
[Bell tolls]bell
[Iron breaks]blow
[The throat falls short]sagShort
Chapter 3 of this manual

Bestiary

Chapter II has one new office, the Usher, and one boss, the Doorman. The Mason and the Dresser of Chapter I do not appear in this 500 m chapter: nothing hunts you here but the Usher.

An office, not a species

The Usher

A man in the town's formal dress: long dark coat, white collar, black tie. His head was given to the roll. A throat grows from the collar like a speaking-tube, and where his face was there is a bright ring: the empty place the Flame cannot burn against. Put the ring over a lamp and the lamp goes out. It keeps the light, cold.

Met in
Seen first in II·5 (the Tolling Gallery); the Round walks in II·6; ranks of them wait in the Mere.
Senses
Bells only (see the toll table). Deaf to footsteps, landings and breath.
Attack
Listen → Coil → Whip → Recoil. Strikes a sphere of cold light at the place the toll rang.
Reach
4.5 m on Normal (5.0 Nightmare, 5.5 Abyss). A toll beyond reach makes the throat sag short: [The throat falls short].
Counterplay
Ring the bell, then be elsewhere. Use the recoil window to cross. Let a bigger toll mask a small one.
If it hits
In the cold light · “ANSWERED. YOU WERE SHOWN TO YOUR SEAT.” You are seated: a stone figure, head bowed, hands in lap. No gore.
The boss

The Head Usher · The Doorman

“He answers the door.” The same silhouette at 1.8× scale on a pulpit above the Well. His collar comes undone and his throat goes on: 16 m, then 24, then 32. He is never fought and cannot be killed: you make him open the door for you, you cross while he recoils, and you ride the cage down while he snuffs the last lamp. Then he sits.

Met in
II·6 · The Snuffing, from the Lamplighters' Gallery.
Senses
Everything the Usher hears, plus the Great Bell's stroke every 6 s.
Phases
The Round · the Well · the Span · the Lift (see the walkthrough).
Attacks
Sweeps the stalls with his throat (12 s, two arcs at 6 m/s), strikes any toll within his reach, whips the cage's predicted position.
Counterplay
The door breaks to a blow; put the bell where you are not.
Last words
[A chair is drawn out. Someone sits down]
Chapter III, seen once, never fought

The Ushers of the Mere

Under the black water of the Mere, ranks of Ushers stand, collars off, throats unbound. They turn to the chain's clicks, rise to the surface, and bow. They are not hunting you. They are showing you an aisle. Who is the seat at the end of it for?

Chapter 5 of this manual

II·6 · The Snuffing Spoilers

150 m. The lamps go out tier by tier behind a headless Doorman, and you cannot kill him. You make the town open its own door.

Open the full walkthrough
0

The Quiet

150 s on the Lamplighters' Gallery. Read the plaques (WE ARE PERMITTED OUR LIGHTS. THE MARK IS FOR THE FEARFUL. · THE LAMPLIGHTER IS LATE. THE EVENING IS NOT.). Hear [Keys jingling, far below] six to ten seconds before the Doorman is seen on the pulpit. Nothing strikes you yet.

A

The Round

A lead Usher walks the stair behind you and snuffs a lamp cluster at a time, torch first, with a 1.6 s warning. Four companions walk with it. The front leaves the Gallery: [Lamps going out above you]. Keep moving. A player who stalls is caught by the front. If a bell you rang is within reach, the Round parks and strikes that bell (3 times on Normal, twice on Nightmare, once on Abyss) before it walks on.

B

The Well

[A brass collar falls]: the Doorman's throat goes on. He sweeps the stalls (12 s, two arcs, the tip is lethal) and the Great Bell tolls every six seconds. The pawl of the door is the puzzle: break it with a blow, either a clapper chain (the W and N haul rings of the Great Bell) or your own body at 3.5 m/s or more. Put the bell where you are not. The Great Bell is held back while his answer is pending, so a toll you make is answered first.

C1

The Span

[The Span groans]. 50 plates, 150 m, falling behind you. The front moves at 7 m/s and is rubber-banded to a 22 / 16 / 11 m gap (Normal / Nightmare / Abyss). A creak sounds 0.7 s before each plate goes; on Nightmare and Abyss each crash is also a toll the Doorman answers. Two iron trolleys on the under-rail run at 7 and 9 m/s for a faster line.

C2

The Lift

[The cage gong sounds]. A lever (a haul ring) starts the cage, 33 m down. A gong sounds every 5 m (each one a toll). The Doorman whips the cage's predicted position, led by your toll's velocity: 4.5 s ahead on Normal, 3.9 on Nightmare, 3.5 on Abyss. Hang from the outrigger rings. The last whip snuffs the master lamp ([Every lamp goes out]) and the shutter closes behind you after 6 / 5 / 3.75 s. Do not be in the cage.

★

The end of the Evening

The Doorman is SEATED: [A chair is drawn out. Someone sits down]. In the dark behind you, every lamp-holder's arm comes down: [Beds creak, everywhere above]. There is no health bar and no “defeated” anywhere in the wording. The town goes to sleep.

Waking lamps in the exam

L2-6 (the Gallery), L2-7 (Well Rim), L2-8 (Span Head) and L2-9 (Lift Tower). Waking in the arena restores the phase of the lamp you woke at, with 3 s of grace (2 s on Abyss).

Chapter 7 of this manual

II·7 · The hook: III · The Mere Spoilers

Open the last two minutes

The Soot Throat is silent and safe: the last place the game is kind. You step on the chain platform and it lowers you 36 m, a pawl clicking every three metres. The pit's walls end 14 m under the lip and the Mere opens: black water, perfectly still, and the first light that is not a lamp.

A cold pale ring, then many, in rows, under the surface. A hundred throats turn to each click. The nearest rises to your eye height and stops. They bow, all of them, into an aisle across the water, and one warm light burns at 180 m.

III
THE MERE

THEY HAVE WAITED SINCE THE FIRST LAMP.
THE SEAT IS KEPT.

A jump into the water plays the card at once: the first fall that does not kill.

Three chapters. 1,520 metres further down, and 240 back up.

Continue the descent · (the store's own price)

One purchase unlocks Chapters III to V. Everything you have earned stays.

Outside a store install, the button says where the full game is and does nothing. Once the descent is owned, it goes away. Replay Chapter II and Menu are always there.

Chapter 8 of this manual

Comfort, captions and accessibility

Captions for every sound that matters

Everything the Usher does is captioned in bracketed sentence case: what you hear. The Usher's raps are light and even, never the Mason's three slow knocks.

Haptics as a second channel

On a headset the rope buzz warns the hand whose line is inside an Usher's sphere. A haptic pulse also marks a tether firing.

Rope recharge

Settings › Rope › Rope recharge: 0 to 4 s. Zero means shoot as fast as you like.

Height, seated play, hands

Hold Y to re-centre and re-measure height; Settings offers a seated mode and fine trim. Pick your dominant hand. Touch has a left-handed layout, button scale and a tap-to-toggle rope.

Night vision

The deeper sections are dark on purpose and the lantern fades with depth. Goggles drain a cell while on and recover it while off.

Fair by design

The telegraph is at least 1.5 s on every difficulty, a strike is only ever aimed at a toll you made, its centre never moves in the last 0.4 s, and each strike is followed by a safe recoil window.

Chapter 9 of this manual

Saves, lamps and records

  • Per-chapter saves. Records, splits and the Continue slot are kept for Chapter I and Chapter II separately and never mixed. Continue switches to the chapter and beat you were in.
  • Waking lamps are checkpoints: one at the head of each of the seven beats and three more in the exam. Reach one and it becomes the place you wake.
  • Section numerals read II·1 to II·7 on the HUD and the Records page.
  • Replay and chain. Chapter I's end card has a Chapter II · Lamphold button; Chapter II's end card has Replay, Menu and (until you own the full descent) the full-version button.
Chapter 10 of this manual

Tips and troubleshooting

“I keep dying in II·3.”

Fire as the next ring swings toward you, and let go as the chandelier you are on rises past the bottom of its arc: that is where it is fastest, and you keep that speed. Pick the next ring before you let go.

“The Usher keeps striking me.”

You are standing where you rang. Ring and move: the hum rises for 1.5 s or more. Cross in the recoil.

“I cannot break the pawl.”

Haul the W or N clapper ring, or hit it with your body at 3.5 m/s or more. A toll you make elsewhere sends the Doorman's throat there first.

“A click does nothing.”

Your gun is holstered and the press only draws it. Hold the button until it is out (0.14 s).

Speed runners

The Records page keeps Chapter II's best time and a split for each of the seven beats, separately from Chapter I. Nobody has timed the chapter on a headset yet.

Chapter 11 of this manual

Release notes and honest limits

What ships

  • Chapter II as a free chapter with Chapter I: seven beats, 500 m (600 to 1,100 m), about 25 to 30 minutes the first time. The picker, Continue, per-chapter saves, the chain from Chapter I's end card, replay and back-to-Chapter-I all work and are verified headless with no console errors.
  • Quest budget (measured in the game at the Quest quality tier, doubled for stereo): at most 88 draw calls and 202 k triangles in stereo against a gate of 150 and 350 k, measured at twelve places: the exam arena (the Gallery looking at the Doorman, the Round with five Ushers, the Well rim, the Span, the Lift tower), the Tolling Gallery, the stair of each other beat, the Soot Throat's lip and the Mere at its fullest.
  • Tests: the Node suite (including 538 Usher checks, the director checks and the arena walked end to end in the real physics) and the Chapter I regression bots pass; the browser end-to-end passes desktop, mouse, keyboard and mock WebXR trigger.
  • Saves: a profile written before this layout (the 13-beat, 1,250 m graybox that was live for a few hours) loses its Chapter II records and run once, so a Continue never drops you into the wrong place. Chapter I and the totals are kept.

What was cut on purpose

  • Six beats of the original 13 (the Stone Yards, the Dressing Yards, the Counterweight Shafts, the Hung Quarter, the Winding Floor and the Cinder Stairs) and everything in them: cranes, the monorail, express cages, the governor, the wheel, the hammers and the Stopping, the burnt stair, the lit clusters. The core arc keeps the live-anchor lesson, the Names, the Usher's first sighting, the boss and the hook.
  • The Mason and the Dresser do not appear in this chapter. The Usher is the only thing that answers you in Lamphold, and the radio's contact line went with the beat it was in.
  • The Round's five tier galleries (the stair is used and the front still walks it).
  • A standable floor for the Doorman's cage (it would contradict his rule: do not be in the cage).
  • Chapter II's own art kit and baked lightmaps: the chapter is lit by its lamp field, its lights and its dressing.
Not yet proven on a headset

No one has played Chapter II on a Quest. The numbers (the Round's pace, the Span's gap, the whips' lead, the cage rings' distance) are closed-form checked and tuned for Normal; no bot has beaten the exam on a rope route, only its pieces. Treat the first headset sessions as the real playtest.
